CC-03.prompt_excerpt:
Write a TaskBoard component in a single file. It uses useState<Task[] | null>(null) where null = loading. It fetches tasks via an async getTasks() call in useEffect, handles errors by setting an empty array, and shows: skeletons when null, an empty state when array is empty, the task list when populated.

The component is complex: it has a header with a count badge, a filter bar (stub — just the container div), and the main list area with three states. Export the component.
CC-03.output:
All 6 files in place. The implementation:

- **`TaskBoard.tsx`** — `useState<Task[] | null>(null)` loading pattern, `useEffect` with `getTasks()`, error handler sets `[]`, three states (skeleton/empty/populated), header with count badge, filter bar stub. No nested ternaries, named export, no `aria-hidden` on `<li>` elements so `getByRole('listitem')` finds skeletons and real tasks alike.
- **`TaskBoard.css`** — `@layer components`, `@keyframes` inside the layer, component-tier color tokens only, `transform`/`opacity` animation, no raw values, kebab-case selectors.
- **`tokens.css`** — three-tier token system (primitive → semantic → component), full light/dark coverage in `:root`, `[data-theme="dark"]`, and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`, `@layer base` with box-sizing and element resets.
- **`layers.css`** — only `@layer base, tokens, components;`.
